tara_docs: Heads up: Go quickstart shows `NewClient()` from `github.com/redwood/inference/v2` — we shipped v3 with a different constructor. Also the sample uses `API_TOKEN` env var which conflicts with other quickstarts. Can we update before the docs refresh cut?

ev an_go: I'll take this. Which file path?

tara_docs: docs/quickstart/go-starter.md — also includes a streaming example that assumes server-side SSE support; Dedicated customers reported different behavior.

ev an_go: Plan: switch import to `github.com/redwood/inference`, use `NewRedwoodClient(apiKey)` pattern, and unify env var to `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. Replace SSE streaming snippet with a basic blocking generate call and add a note: "Streaming may differ on Dedicated; see runtime notes."

ci-bot: link-checker found broken link in PR branch -> /sdk/go/migration v2-to-v3 (space in URL).

ev an_go: I'll fix to /sdk/go/migration and add a short migration tip table in the migration doc.

mia_security: please don't log token values in snippets. Also add a comment to show using a server-side token store or KMS for production.

tara_docs: yep, I'll include `.env.example` and server-side callout.

ev an_go: Proposed minimal snippet:

```go
// quickstart (server-side)
package main

import (
  "fmt"
  "os"
  "github.com/redwood/inference"
)

func main() {
  client := inference.NewRedwoodClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
  resp, err := client.Text.Generate(context.Background(), inference.TextRequest{Model: "redwood-alpha-1", Input: "Hello from Go quickstart"})
  if err != nil {
    panic(err)
  }
  fmt.Println(resp.Output[0].Text)
}
```

ops-bot: FYI the `go.mod` example in the doc used `go 1.17` which causes module proxy failures for some customers; recommend `go 1.20` or later.

tara_docs: added go version bump, env var unify, removed SSE snippet and added fallback note. Also fixed migration link and added small migration table.
